claims.claim: FY2026 Q4 revenue reached $90.0B, up 18% YoY, while Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $59.3B, up 27%; Azure annual revenue surpassed $100B and Microsoft 365 Copilot exceeded 30M paid seats.
Commercial remaining performance obligations reached $678B, with growth extending beyond frontier-model customers, a strong forward-demand signal for cloud and AI infrastructure.

risks.risk: AI infrastructure intensity is depressing cloud gross margin and free cash flow conversion relative to operating cash flow.

unknowns.unknown: Return on the current AI infrastructure investment wave is not yet separable from broader Azure economics.

claims.claim: Execution is strong: Q4 revenue and operating income both rose 18%, Microsoft Cloud grew 27%, and commercial RPO provides substantial contracted visibility.
The principal expectation risk is that very high AI capex must convert into durable Azure/Copilot economics while cloud gross margin absorbs infrastructure investment.

risks.risk: Capex intensity and concentration of AI infrastructure commitments can pressure near-term returns if demand conversion slows.

unknowns.unknown: Current artifact does not establish a market valuation entry point.
